targetName: Expedition Ship Bespoke Lower Deck Interior Systems

terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: The source is a four-panel concept authority for a fabrication garage and a multispecies sanctuary inside the already-approved controller-shaped expedition ship. Hidden dimensions are approximate; the existing ship envelope and floor allocation remain fixed.

reasoning: Two different occupied pressure-room environments must remain coherent with one established transforming ship.
The workshop depends on continuous perimeter machinery, articulated equipment and repeated tool/storage bays rather than a few standalone primitives.
The sanctuary depends on linked terrain, water, upholstery, privacy arches and vegetation across several height bands.
Multiple PBR families, heavy occlusion and live interior camera movement make the target ultra-complex despite the fixed room envelopes.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Choose simple/moderate/complex/ultra-complex from observed structure, not from a hardcoded domain.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Concentric suspended maintenance rings with radial braces over the garage lift.
Continuous perimeter cabinets, shelves, tool bays and warm task-light reveals.
Transparent cyan engine diagnostic volume above a curved technical desk.
Socketed multi-link robotic arms with visible rotary joints and tool heads.
Layered circular service platform with recessed radial channels and warm rim light.
Parallel service trenches, clamp pads and luminous guide strips around vehicle bays.
Warm bronze/wood-toned curved worktop edge against dark metal cabinetry.
Narrow warm light strips inset beneath shelves and inside tool bays.
Several shallow cyan-green basins connected by narrow rills and low falls.
Thick rounded lounge and nest pads in several creature scales.
Repeated circular and half-ring privacy frames embedded into planted banks.
Ground cover, shrubs, trailing plants and upper-edge foliage in distinct height bands.
Rounded coping and stepping stones break the hard basin edges.
Thick cushion profiles and inset seams distinguish upholstery from terrain.
Restrained warm lights follow selected pool and furniture edges.
Low-tint pressure glazing surrounds the occupied rooms without reading as opaque walls.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: Fabrication POV reads as a contained vehicle-scale engineering garage with continuous perimeter machinery, rotary service lift, overhead maintenance structure and articulated service equipment.
Creature-habitat POV reads as a contained multispecies sanctuary landscape with linked water, curved residences, thick upholstery and planting in multiple height bands.
Both rooms remain inside the approved controller-shaped expedition ship, preserve the existing storey allocation and do not intrude into the Great Tree volume.
The High tier remains at or below 72,000 triangles and 160 meshes while retaining drag-look interior cameras.

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.

colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

The reference reads as a dense luxury engineering yacht and lush multispecies sanctuary; the render still reads as an early procedural blockout with oversimplified equipment, sparse ecology, weak PBR response and dark ceiling planes. visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: The corrected comparison—not the earlier accidental atrium capture—is authoritative. Density and bronze separation improve slightly over checkpoint 29, but the workshop still reads as an early procedural blockout: a broad dark service floor, repeated cone-like stations, simplified gantry pieces, limited PBR response and weak architectural lighting. Sanctuary systems improve modestly but remain similarly early. The multi-angle volume check passes; the Tier-1 0.8207 IoU failure is recorded and remains partly framing-sensitive, while the semantic gap is visibly much larger than that number suggests.

featureReviews.notes: Cabinet and worktop replacement creates a more coherent perimeter, but density and finish remain coarse.
Diagnostic ring and existing gantry give clearer engineering semantics without reference-level articulated machinery.
Garage bleed is removed and greenery reads continuously, but the ground remains flat and under-articulated.

visualEvidence.cameraView: fabrication primary plus genuine dragged yaw; creature sanctuary; Haven and Fast Space regression
visualEvidence.notes: Real structural improvement, still well below visual acceptance.
visualEvidence.aiVisionNotes: Compared with checkpoint 30, the workshop gains a visible service floor, coherent rectangular stations and a restrained cyan diagnostic display; the sanctuary also loses the orange workshop intrusion. The comparison still shows a very large semantic gap: the reference is dense, reflective, layered and cinematic, while the render has broad flat planes, sparse primitive machinery, weak lighting and little PBR response. The yawed image proves non-degenerate 3D volume (area ratio 0.8348) but also reveals that the room envelope is not fully authored. Tier-1 fails at IoU 0.821 and missing map-stripped evidence; this is framing-sensitive but consistent with the visible blockout-level mismatch.
